status_note: Still open on main (a4d8e00342d0): [`functions_string.yaml` L985-L1037](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_string.yaml#L985-L1037) point `lower`/`upper` at the utf8_unicode_ci collation and return `varchar<L1>` for `varchar<L1>`, with nothing on simple or full case mapping; the test cases are ASCII only. No existing issue.
summary: `upper` and `lower` with `char_set: UTF8` say the implementation "should follow the utf8_unicode_ci collations" of the Unicode Collation Algorithm (UTR #10), which is a collation, not a case mapping. Nothing says whether the mapping is Unicode's simple one (one code point to one, the length kept) or the full one of SpecialCasing.txt (`ß` to `SS`, `ﬁ` to `FI`, `İ` to `i̇`, a final sigma). Engines differ: DuckDB maps code point by code point, Rust's `str::to_uppercase` (Polars, DataFusion) maps in full. The `varchar<L1>` and `fixedchar<L1>` signatures return the input's length, which a full mapping can exceed.
repro: `upper('ß')`: DuckDB 2.0.0 gives `ẞ` (U+1E9E), Polars 2.1.0 gives `SS`. `lower('ΣΑΣ')`: DuckDB `σασ`, Polars `σας`. `upper('ﬁ')`: DuckDB `ﬁ`, Polars `FI`. `lower('İ')`: DuckDB `i` (one character), Polars `i̇` (two).
handling: The reference defines `upper` and `lower` as black boxes with Rust's full mappings (`Text.upper`, `Text.lower`), and the written SQL raises on non-ASCII text for every engine (`ascii_only`, #70), where every engine agrees.
Could be expressed as: a `case_mapping` option (`SIMPLE`, `FULL`) beside `char_set`, or `UTF8` defined as one of the two, with the length rule for the `varchar<L1>` and `fixedchar<L1>` signatures.
